A.subject: Physics
A.text: A large tank of cross-section are A contains liquid of density ρ. A cylinder of density ρ/4 and length l and cross-section area a (a << A) is kept in equilibrium by applying an external vertically downward force as shown. The cylinder is just submerged in liquid. At t = 0 the external force is removed instantaneously. Assume that water level in the tank remains constant. The velocity of the cylinder when it reaches its equilibrium position is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Hint:
V = Aω
Solution:
The density of liquid is four times that of cylinder, hence in equilibrium position one fourth of the cylinder will remain submerged. So as the cylinder is released from initial position it moves distance (3l/4) to reach its equilibrium position. The upward motion in this duration is SHM.
Therefore attained velocity is V_max = Aω

where, ω = √(4g/l) and A = 3l/4

Thus, V_max = (3/2)√(gl)

A.text: An ideal liquid is filled in a cylindrical container of area of cross-section A. There is a circular hole of area (A/4) at the bottom. If the hole is opened then the estimate of acceleration (using Bernoulli's theorem) with which the surface of the liquid will fall is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (3)
Solution:
Av = (A/4)v₀ ⇒ v = v₀/4
v₀ = velocity of efflux
v = velocity of the surface
(1/2)ρv² + ρgH = (1/2)ρv₀²
⇒ 2gH = 16v² - v²
⇒ v² = 2gH/15 ⇒ a = g/15

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A uniform rod of mass m and length L with a particle of mass m attached at its one end is released from horizontal position. The other end of rod is hinged. If Young's modulus of rod is Y, then total elongation in rod when it becomes vertical is (A is cross-sectional area of rod
A.sol_text:
Using work energy theorem
(1/2)Iω² + (1/2)m(ωl)² = mg(L/2) + mgl
(1/2)(ml²/3)ω² + (1/2)mω²l² = (3/2)mgl
mℓ²ω²(2/3) = (3/2)mgl
ω = √(9g/(4l)) ⇒ ω = (3/2)√(g/l)

T = (m/L)ωx²(L - x + x/2) + (m + m/L x)g + mω²L
= (m/L)ω²(Lx - x²/2) + m(ω²L + g) + (m/L)gx

Stress = T/A = (mω²/A)(x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + g/ω² · x/L)

Strain at this location = dl/dx

dl/dx = (mω²/YA)(x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + g/ω² · x/L)

∫dl = (mω²/YA)∫(x - x²/(2L) + L + g/ω² + g/ω² · x/L)dx

Δl = (mω²L/YA)(4/3 L + 3g/(2ω²)) = (9MgL)/(2AY)

A.subject: Physics
A.text:
The specific heat capacity of a metal at low temperature (T) is given as
C_p (kJ·K^(-1) kg^(-1)) = 32(T/400)^3
A 100 gram vessel of this metal is to be cooled from 20°K to 4°K by a special refrigerator operating at room temperature (27°C). The amount of work required to cool the vessel is
A.sol_text:
Heat energy required = m ∫_T₁^T₂ c dT
= ∫_4^20 0.1 × 32(T/400)^3 dT
≃ 0.002 kJ
Now, refrigerator is working at 27°C (= 300 K).
Now, if the temperature remains constant at 20°K, then work done by refrigerator
= Q(T₁-T₂)/T₂
= (0.002)(300-20)/20
= 0.028 kJ
Work done by refrigerator if temperature remains constant at 4°K
= (0.002)(300-4)/4
= 0.148 kJ
As the temperature is varying from 20°K → 4°K, thus the work by refrigerator will be between 0.148 kJ and 0.028 kJ.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A rigid box contains one mole of an ideal gas of molar heat capacity at constant volume C. The walls of the box have total surface area A, thickness t₀ and thermal conductivity K. Initially the gas is at a temperature T₀ and pressure P₀. The temperature of the surrounding is T₀/2. The temperature of gas as a function of time, is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Hint:
dQ/dt = C dT/dt

Solution:
dQ/dt = C dT/dt ...(i)
dQ/dt = (KA/t₀)(T - T₀/2) ...(ii)

From equation (i) and equation (ii)
C dT/dt = -(KA/t₀)(T - T₀/2)

⇒ ∫_{T₀}^T [C dt/(T - T₀/2)] = ∫_0^t [-(KA/t₀)] dt

⇒ T = (T₀/2)(1 + e^(-KAt/t₀))

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The figure given below shows pressure versus volume (P – V) graph for a process. The volume of the ideal gas changes by n times within the cycle. The efficiency of a cycle consisting of two isochoric and two adiabatic processes is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)
Solution:
Process 1 → 2 and 3 → 4 is isochoric
Q₁₂ = nC_v(T₂ − T₁)
Q₃₄ = nC_v(T₃ − T₄)
η = (Q₁₂ − Q₃₄)/Q₁₂ = (nC_v[(T₂−T₁)−(T₃−T₄)])/(nC_v(T₂−T₁))
η = 1 − (T₃−T₄)/(T₂−T₁)
For adiabatic process
T₂V₀^(γ−1) = T₃(nV₀)^(γ−1)
T₁V₀^(γ−1) = T₄(nV₀)^(γ−1)
⇒ (T₂ − T₁)V₀^(γ−1) = (T₃ − T₄)(nV₀)^(γ−1)
(T₃−T₄)/(T₂−T₁) = 1/n^(γ−1)
η = 1 − 1/(n^(γ−1))

At equilibrium position,

After collision m₂ sticks to m₁

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
Consider the following compound of sulphur
(a) H₂SO₄
(b) H₂SO₅
(c) H₂S₂O₈
(d) Na₂S₂O₆

Select the correct statement.

(1) Oxidation number of sulphur in (b) is +7
(2) Oxidation number of sulphur in (a), (b), and (c) are same and +6
(3) Oxidation number of each sulphur atom in (d) is same
(4) In (c), each oxygen atom has −2 oxidation state
options: Oxidation number of sulphur in (b) is +7
Oxidation number of sulphur in (a), (b), and (c) are same and +6
Oxidation number of each sulphur atom in (d) is same
In (c), each oxygen atom has −2 oxidation state
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)

Solution:

H₂SO₄ → +6 S
        S structure shows oxygen double bonded to S with two O-H groups

H₂SO₅ → sulfur structure shows one oxygen double bonded to S with three O-H/O groups

Na₂S₂O₆ → structure shows two sulfur atoms connected, with different oxidation states marked as +5 S and 0 S, with Na⁺ and O²⁻ groups

For H₂SO₄:
Let oxidation number of S = x
2(+1) + x + 4(−2) = 0
2 + x − 8 = 0
x = +6

For H₂SO₅:
Let oxidation number of S = x
2(+1) + x + 5(−2) = 0
2 + x − 10 = 0
x = +8

For H₂S₂O₈:
Let oxidation number of each S = x
2(+1) + 2x + 8(−2) = 0
2 + 2x − 16 = 0
2x = 14
x = +7

For Na₂S₂O₆:
Na = +1, O = −2
2(+1) + 2x + 6(−2) = 0
2 + 2x − 12 = 0
2x = 10
x = +5 (average)

But the sulphur atoms are not equivalent. One has +5 and one has 0.

Statement (2) is INCORRECT because oxidation numbers are: (a) = +6, (b) = +8, (c) = +7

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
Match the List-I with List-II

List-I
Reaction

(a) Alkyne + Lindlar's catalyst
(b) Alkyne + Sodium and liq. NH₃
(c) 2-Bromobutane + alcoholic KOH
(d) 2-Bromobutane + aqueous KOH

List II
Major Products

(i) trans-alkene
(ii) cis-alkene
(iii) Butan-2-ol
(iv) But-2-ene
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Solution:

(a) Alkyne + Lindlar's catalyst → cis-alkene (ii)
The mechanism shows: R—C≡C—R' with Pd/C and Lindlar's Catalyst produces the structure with H and R on one side, and H and R' on the other side in a cis configuration.

(b) Alkyne + Na/liq. NH₃ → trans-alkene (i)
The mechanism shows: R—C≡C—R' with Na/liq. NH₃ produces the structure with H and R' on one side, and H and R on the other side in a trans configuration.

(c) 2-Bromobutane + alcoholic KOH → But-2-ene (iv) (major)
The mechanism shows: CH₃—CH—CH₂—CH₃ with Br substituted at the second carbon, treated with alc. KOH, produces CH₃—CH=CH—CH₃ (major product) via elimination.

(d) 2-Bromobutane + aqueous KOH → Butan-2-ol (iii) (major)
The mechanism shows: CH₃—CH—CH₂—CH₃ with Br substituted at the second carbon, treated with aq. KOH, produces CH₃—CH—CH₂—CH₃ with OH substituted at the second carbon (major product) via SN₂ substitution.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Heating of 2-Chloro-1-phenylbutane with EtOK/EtOH gives X as the major product. Reaction of X with Hg(OAc)₂/H₂O followed by NaBH₄ gives Y as the major product. Y is:
options: OH with Ph attached to left carbon and propyl chain to right, with OH on the left carbon
Ph with propyl chain, OH on middle carbon of the chain
OH on terminal carbon, Ph and ethyl chain attached to adjacent carbon
Ph with butyl chain, no OH group
A.sol_text:
Heating of 2-Chloro-1-phenylbutane with EtOK/EtOH → Major product X is formed via elimination (Hofmann or Zaitsev mechanism)

Starting material: 2-Chloro-1-phenylbutane with Cl at position 2

Elimination gives X as the alkene: (CH₃CH₂)C=CH-Ph (2-phenylbutene/1-phenyl-1-butene)

Reaction of X with (i) (CH₃COO)₂Hg + H₂O, (ii) NaBH₄ (OMDM reaction - Oxymercuration-Demercuration):

This is a Markovnikov's addition of water to the alkene:
- Hg(OAc)₂/H₂O adds to the alkene, forming a mercurinium ion
- Water attacks (Markovnikov's rule: OH adds to the more substituted carbon)
- NaBH₄ reduces to give the alcohol

The OH group adds to the more substituted carbon of the double bond (the carbon bearing the phenyl group), giving:

1-phenylbutanol (Ph-CH(OH)-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃)

Structure: Carbon 1 has Ph and OH, carbons 2-4 form the propyl chain

Product Y is option (1): 1-phenylbutanol with OH at the carbon attached to Ph

max(LR) → ∞ as θ → π/2
